messages:
devon: Running a helm upgrade of gpupool chart (v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0) in eu-west-1, post-upgrade hook job is failing and blocking the rollout. Logs show conntrack / SNAT exhaustion errors. Anyone seen this during large canaries?

miguel: Can you paste the job logs and the hook manifest?

devon: Logs (kubectl logs -n infra gpupool-hook-xyz):

  2026-02-26T14:12:03Z ERROR dial tcp 10.0.2.15:443: connect: connection refused
  2026-02-26T14:12:03Z WARN  netfilter: could not create conntrack entry: table full
  2026-02-26T14:12:03Z ERROR transient network failure: conntrack: table full
  2026-02-26T14:12:35Z FATAL hook timed out after 300s

Also seeing kernel dmesg on node: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet"

devon: Hook job is a parallel Job that probes the model registry / internal-metadata service for ~200 hosts concurrently as part of warmup. It spikes outbound SNATs.

sara: That sounds like we exhausted nf_conntrack on the node pool. eu-west gpupool nodes are smaller (c6g.medium-ish) and have low default conntrack limits. Did the hook increase parallelism recently? :thinking:

anna: We had a similar issue during the last model rollout when the warmup job hit registry and metrics endpoints in parallel. We solved it by reducing parallelism + tuning sysctl.

miguel: Quick checks you can run on the node: 
  cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
  cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
If count ~= max you're hitting the limit.

devon: Ran those on one node: count=98304 max=131072 (so ~75% but spikes push over). We saw NAT port exhaustion on kube-proxy for ephemeral ports too.

infra-bot: [alert] metric nf_conntrack_used on gpupool-nodes-eu-west crossed 80% at 2026-02-26T14:11:58Z. Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/rp/gpupool-overview

sara: Short-term mitigation: 1) scale gpupool nodegroup by +20% to spread connections 2) reduce hook job parallelism to 4 (from 200) 3) add preflight check in the GitOps pipeline to abort upgrade if conntrack_used > 70%

anna: Long-term: push a Terraform change to bump nf_conntrack_max in the node user-data (sysctl) or bake tuned kernel settings into our AMI. Also consider enabling connection pooling in the warmup tool instead of per-host fresh connections.

miguel: Suggested helm changes: make the warmup hook a Job with 
  parallelism: 4
  completions: 200
and add backoffLimit: 2. Also mark it as "helm.sh/hook-weight: 5" so it runs after smaller hooks. Example snippet: 

  apiVersion: batch/v1
  kind: Job
  metadata:
    annotations:
      "helm.sh/hook": post-upgrade
  spec:
    parallelism: 4
    completions: 200
    template:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: warmup
          image: registry.redwood/warmup:stable
          env:
          - name: WARMUP_CONCURRENCY
            value: "4"

miguel: Also proposing a pre-upgrade CI step in our gitops pipeline: run a quick check against the Prometheus endpoint and fail fast if nf_conntrack_used > 70%. We can implement that as a tiny container step.

devon: Rolling back now (helm rollback) to unblock prod. Will follow up with the limited-parallelism PR.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback gpupool/production -> v2.3.1 triggered by @devon at 2026-02-26T14:19:12Z :white_check_mark:

anna: For the infra TF PR: we should add a sysctl module that writes /etc/sysctl.d/99-nf.conf with: 
  net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 262144
and ensure we drain/recreate nodes via rolling update. Beware of cost bump + ephemeral port math (adjust net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports if needed).

sara: Cost/region note: eu-west nodes are smaller and we can't just double size without budget signoff. Let's prefer chart-level mitigations first (reduce concurrency) and preflight check. If we still see repeated incidents, then request capacity bump with finance cc.

devon: Action items:
  - miguel: PR to chart to reduce hook concurrency + add backoff (in progress)
  - anna: TF PR draft to expose nf_conntrack_max via node user-data (will open tomorrow)
  - sara: Add preflight check to gitops pipeline and a runbook note for conntrack checks

miguel: I'll also add a small retry/backoff in the warmup script (exponential sleep) so we don't hammer the registry during transient blips.

devon: thanks. Will post the helm PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: created ticket INF-4821 "gpupool helm hook conntrack exhaustion" and linked to rollback event.

sara: if anyone is curious, quick debug tip: on a node you can dump conntrack table count per proto with: 
  sudo conntrack -S | grep entries | awk '{print $2,$3}'

miguel: one more thought — we should also consider running warmup jobs on a control plane-only pool that has larger sysctl limits (no GPU attach), then register the warmed hosts into gpupool asynchronously. Avoids touching GPU nodes' conntrack budget during helm operations.

devon: good idea. I'll add that as a follow-up to the PR.

ops-bot: note: thread archived into INF-4821 at 2026-02-26T14:22:01Z

sara: cool, thanks everyone. Keep the updates here so oncall can follow. :eyes:
